name: Alabama
publisher: Alabama Department of Environmental Management, Alabama Forestry Commission and local authorities

extraUrls.label: State wildfire orders and prescribed-burn permit law
Cahaba Valley Fire District burn status and permits

notes: Alabama limits land-clearing fires statewide. Twelve counties have tighter rules from May through October, and Jefferson County has separate rules. The State Forester can issue wildfire alerts, and the Forestry Commission can declare wildfire emergencies with the Governor’s approval. For current orders and prescribed-burn permits, call Forestry at 800-392-5679 and check with your local fire authority.

name: Alaska
publisher: Alaska Division of Forestry & Fire Protection and Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation

extraUrls.label: DEC winter open-burning rules and maps

notes: State Forestry generally requires burn permits April 1 through August 31 and can suspend permits by zone or order emergency closures. Alaska DEC and local agencies issue separate restrictions for some cities, fire service areas and air-quality zones. Check the linked jurisdiction and your land manager for the rules at your address.

name: Arizona
publisher: Arizona Department of Forestry and Fire Management, Pima County, and National Park Service

extraUrls.label: Grand Canyon National Park fire restrictions
Maricopa County air quality burning rules and No Burn Days
Area A boundaries in Maricopa, Pinal and Yavapai counties

notes: The state forestry department covers State Trust lands, and counties, cities, fire districts, tribes and federal agencies issue restrictions for their own areas. Air quality rules also apply, including Maricopa County No Burn Days and summer open-burning limits in parts of Maricopa, Pinal and Yavapai counties.

name: Arkansas
publisher: Arkansas Department of Agriculture, Forestry Division
notes: County judges issue and lift burn bans. The Forestry Division publishes reported county orders on its map. The site checks available county notices and local restrictions. Check the county judge or local fire department for the rules at your address. Contact the land manager for rules on public lands. State air-quality rules also apply.

name: California
publisher: CAL FIRE

extraUrls.label: CARB agricultural and prescribed burn decisions
San Joaquin Valley hazard-reduction burn declarations
Bay Area open burning rules and notices

notes: County entries include local fire and air district decisions and standing rules. Each report names the covered activity and area. Check both authorities at the burn site for permit requirements and any current orders.

name: Colorado
publisher: Local Colorado fire authorities and the Air Pollution Control Division

extraUrls.label: Colorado BLM fire restrictions and closures
El Paso County Sheriff fire information
Larimer County fire danger and restrictions
Estes Valley Fire Protection District restrictions

notes: County sheriffs and commissioners, municipalities, fire districts, and federal land managers can issue restrictions for their own areas. County entries include local orders, standing permit rules and Denver-area indoor wood-burning advisories. Check your local fire authority, land manager and air-quality rules for the burn location.

name: Connecticut
publisher: Connecticut DEEP Forestry

extraUrls.label: State park camping and fire rules

notes: Check the dated DEEP fire-danger report and local permit conditions. High fire danger can restrict burning near woodland, brush or adjacent dry grass. Confirm the rule with your town fire authority or land manager.

name: Delaware
publisher: Delaware DNREC Division of Air Quality
notes: Delaware restricts most open burning from May 1 through September 30. The rest of the year, residential brush burning has limits on materials, pile size and hours and requires advance notice to the county fire board. Air Quality Action Days can prohibit all open burning in affected areas. The State Fire Marshal can issue emergency bans by county or statewide. Check with fire officials for current orders at your location.

name: District of Columbia
publisher: DC Department of Energy and Environment

extraUrls.label: DC Parks and Recreation fire and grilling rules

notes: District air rules generally prohibit open fires and allow limited exceptions, including some recreational fires. DC Fire and EMS handles permits for activities such as ceremonial bonfires. The Mayor can issue air-pollution emergency orders. Check with the Fire Marshal about your burn and with the land manager about park restrictions.

name: Florida
publisher: Florida Forest Service
notes: The Florida Forest Service maps county bans and lifts reported voluntarily. Check county and fire district rules and separate statewide or regional orders. Some counties also prohibit yard debris burning.

name: Georgia
publisher: Georgia Environmental Protection Division and local fire authorities

extraUrls.label: Georgia Forestry Commission fire and restrictions map
Georgia Forestry Commission permits and county contacts
Georgia Forestry Commission same-day agricultural and land-clearing permits
Gwinnett Fire Marshal daily burn decision and medical burn zones

notes: Georgia EPD limits certain types of burning in 54 counties May through September and 27 counties October through April. The Georgia Forestry Commission can issue emergency bans. Local fire authorities publish some permit closures and enforce additional rules that can apply to a city, fire district or unincorporated area.

name: Hawaii
publisher: Hawaiʻi Department of Health Clean Air Branch
notes: Hawaiʻi prohibits backyard trash and yard-waste burning year-round. The Clean Air Branch issues agricultural permits and can temporarily stop certain burns in specific districts. Check with your local fire department or land manager for additional orders.

name: Idaho
publisher: Idaho Department of Lands and Idaho DEQ

extraUrls.label: Kootenai County Fire & Rescue burning rules

notes: Land managers issue fire restrictions by zone, and Idaho DEQ issues separate air-quality restrictions. From May 10 through October 20, check state fire-safety permit requirements. Ask your local fire district, city, county, or Tribe about additional rules for your location.

name: Illinois
publisher: Illinois EPA and local authorities

extraUrls.label: Bartlett Fire Protection District burning rules

notes: Illinois limits open burning by material, purpose and location. Cities, counties and fire protection districts can issue separate orders. See coverage for checks on the standing rules and Crawford County orders listed here.

name: Indiana
publisher: Indiana Department of Homeland Security
notes: Indiana DHS maps countywide and local bans reported to it. Check the local issuer for the area covered and IDEM for standing air-quality rules, including residential burning restrictions in Clark, Floyd, Lake and Porter.

name: Iowa
publisher: Iowa State Fire Marshal

extraUrls.label: Iowa DNR open-burning and permit rules

notes: The State Fire Marshal can issue area-specific proclamations at the request of a fire chief, city council or county board. Some county bulletins confirm whether a countywide ban is in effect. Local burn rules and permit requirements can apply separately.

name: Kansas
publisher: Kansas Forest Service, state air-quality regulators and local fire authorities

extraUrls.label: Kansas air-quality rules for open burning
Kansas Forest Service April burning rules
Dickinson County fire-district burn restrictions map
Sedgwick County April burn rules and permit exceptions
Coffey County permit and burn-ban contacts

notes: Kansas air-quality rules limit open burning year-round, with tighter April rules in 16 counties. We also check Dickinson County's fire-district map and Franklin County's permit rules. Contact the local fire authority for temporary orders and permit requirements at your burn site.

name: Kentucky
publisher: Kentucky Division of Forestry

extraUrls.label: Kentucky Division for Air Quality burning rules

notes: County judge-executives and cities can issue local burn bans. The Division of Forestry lists orders reported to it. During spring and fall fire seasons, state law limits daytime burning in or near woods or brush. Check with your county judge-executive or fire department for local orders and exceptions.

name: Louisiana
publisher: Louisiana Department of Agriculture and Forestry
notes: Parishes and municipalities can issue burn bans for all or part of their jurisdiction. The State Fire Marshal can issue separate orders. The LDAF map shows parish reports.

name: Maine
publisher: Maine Forest Service, Maine Legislature and town fire departments

extraUrls.label: Maine Forest Service daily wildfire danger report
Maine Red Flag Warning burning law
Maine Forest Service guidance and ranger contacts

notes: Town forest fire wardens issue permits in organized towns, and Maine Forest Service rangers handle unorganized areas. Maine requires permits for covered open burning and restricts burning during Red Flag Warnings. We also report fire-danger permit limits in Cumberland, South Thomaston, Union and Windham. Ask your local fire warden or ranger about today's rules and permit availability at your address.

name: Maryland
publisher: Maryland DNR Forest Service and Maryland Department of the Environment
notes: Maryland has year-round rules for burning in or near woodland outside incorporated towns. Summer air-quality rules restrict open burning in 11 counties and Baltimore City from June through August. The Governor or DNR can order emergency bans. Check with your local health department or fire marshal for current orders and permits.

name: Massachusetts
publisher: Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection
notes: Residential brush and forestry debris burning is limited to 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. from January 15 through May 1. It is prohibited year-round in 22 cities and towns. Check with your local fire department for a permit and current restrictions. MassDEP can also stop burning because of air quality. Cooking and qualifying agricultural burns have separate rules.

name: Michigan
publisher: Michigan Department of Natural Resources

extraUrls.label: Find a township and its local contacts
State Fire Marshal directory of local fire departments

notes: The DNR reports debris-burning permit conditions in 49 northern counties. Use its county dropdown for township details. Where a county result cites a local fire department or ordinance, check the named city, township or district and the activities it covers. Contact your local fire department for current permits and emergency orders.

name: Minnesota
publisher: Minnesota Department of Natural Resources

extraUrls.label: DNR burning permit rules and exceptions
Permit offices and area maps by county
Superior National Forest alerts and orders

notes: The DNR can suspend permits and restrict open burning in designated areas, including parts of counties. Where verified, county, city, township and Tribal rules appear with the area and activities they cover. Check the DNR map and the local permit issuer or land manager for temporary restrictions at your address.

name: Mississippi
publisher: Mississippi Forestry Commission
notes: County boards request burn bans and the Mississippi Forestry Commission approves them. The table lists start dates, end dates and exemptions when available and readable.

name: Missouri
publisher: Missouri Division of Fire Safety, Show Me Fire and U.S. EPA

extraUrls.label: Show Me Fire’s reported county burn bans
EPA-approved St. Louis metro yard-waste rules
St. Louis County open-burning fact sheet
Wentzville Fire Protection District burning rules

notes: Missouri counties, cities and tax-supported fire protection districts can issue and lift local bans. Show Me Fire publishes reviewed reports. Unreported orders may still apply. The St. Louis metro area has separate rules for burning yard waste. Ask your local fire authority about your address and what you plan to burn.

name: Montana
publisher: Montana DEQ, Montana DNRC and local agencies

extraUrls.label: Montana DEQ open burning seasons and guidance
Flathead County burn permits and activation rules
Participating county permits and daily restrictions

notes: Montana DEQ posts daily fall air-quality limits for open burning in parts of western Montana. Participating counties publish permit closures by county, fire district or zone. Local rules can also require permits or limit when a burn can take place. Tribal, state and federal land managers issue restrictions for their jurisdictions. Check the permit issuer and land manager for your location.

name: Nebraska
publisher: Nebraska Legislature, Nebraska State Fire Marshal and Lincoln-Lancaster County Health Department

extraUrls.label: Lincoln and Lancaster County open-burning rules
Nebraska National Forests and Grasslands alerts
State park campfire bans and advisories

notes: Nebraska limits bonfires, outdoor rubbish fires and land-clearing fires year-round. Local fire chiefs can issue permits or waive the rule for their area. The Governor can suspend permits. Ask the local fire department about current orders, waivers and permits for your burn site. Air-quality and public-land rules can also apply.

name: Nevada
publisher: Nevada Fire Info, Truckee Meadows Fire Protection District and U.S. Forest Service

extraUrls.label: Nevada Division of Forestry state land restrictions
Nevada open-burning permits and smoke rules
Washoe wood-burning device rules and daily hotline

notes: We track daily pile burning in the Truckee Meadows Fire Protection District in part of Washoe County and a campfire order on mapped National Forest lands in part of Clark County. Local fire authorities and air-quality agencies set separate rules. Check the agency that manages the land for current orders.

name: New Hampshire
publisher: New Hampshire General Court and U.S. Forest Service

extraUrls.label: State Forest Protection Bureau fire danger and contacts
State fire permit and suspension rules
White Mountain National Forest alerts and orders

notes: Town forest fire wardens issue open-burning permits and can confirm local rules and suspensions. See coverage for the latest checks on state permit law and the U.S. Forest Service order for part of Carroll County.

name: New Jersey
publisher: New Jersey Forest Fire Service
notes: The Forest Fire Service reports temporary campfire and agricultural burning restrictions by division or county. Local reports describe standing rules within the named municipality or county park system.

name: New Mexico
publisher: New Mexico Forestry, State Parks, state and local air-quality agencies, and Angel Fire Fire Department
notes: State Forestry, local fire authorities, tribes, and federal land managers can issue restrictions in their own jurisdictions. State air-quality rules limit vegetation burning outside Bernalillo County and tribal lands. Albuquerque–Bernalillo has separate open-burning rules. Park and village reports apply only in the named places. Check the fire authority and land manager for your location before burning.

extraUrls.label: State open-burning and smoke management rules
Federal, state and tribal land-manager contacts

name: New York
publisher: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation, NYC 311 and local authorities
notes: New York prohibits residential brush burning March 16 through May 14. Eligible small-town burning has material and size limits, and designated Fire Towns may require permits. NYC and other local authorities can set additional rules.

extraUrls.label: DEC wildfire advisories and burn-ban announcements
DEC Fire Towns and brush-burning permits
NYC Fire Code on open fires

name: North Carolina
publisher: N.C. Forest Service and N.C. Division of Air Quality
notes: The N.C. Forest Service announces state burn bans and lifts. Woodland permits and air-quality burn hours depend on where and what you burn. Check your local fire marshal for local bans, especially within 100 feet of a home that is occupied, and check the county air-quality forecast before burning.

extraUrls.label: Local fire department and fire marshal directory

name: North Dakota
publisher: North Dakota Department of Emergency Services

extraUrls.label: Fire emergency and burn restriction guidance
Fargo recreational fires and bonfire permits

notes: The governor and local governments can issue burn restrictions. The state map shows reported county, city, tribal and land-manager restrictions, often tied to fire danger or a Red Flag Warning. Check with the authority that covers your location and activity.

name: Ohio
publisher: Ohio Division of Forestry
notes: Ohio limits outdoor burning of wood, brush, weeds, grass or rubbish in unincorporated areas from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. Eastern in March through May and October through November. The law has exceptions. The State Fire Marshal and local fire officials can issue additional bans. Check with your local fire department and follow Ohio EPA rules.

extraUrls.label: State Fire Marshal's outdoor fire guide (PDF)
Ohio Fire Code on emergency bans

name: Oklahoma
publisher: Oklahoma Forestry Services
notes: Oklahoma Forestry Services maps reported county resolutions and governor orders. Check the issuing order and any local, tribal or land-manager rules that apply.

publisher: Oregon DEQ, Oregon Department of Forestry and Lane Regional Air Protection Agency

extraUrls.label: Oregon DEQ open burning rules and address map
Before You Burn local fire districts and permits
Lane County home wood heating advisory
Willamette Valley daily open burning announcement
Tualatin Valley Fire and Rescue outdoor burning
BLM fire restrictions on Oregon public lands

notes: Sources include Oregon Department of Forestry orders, Lane County air-quality advisories, the Willamette Valley backyard burning bulletin, and local permit and burn-day restrictions. Check the issuing fire district or agency for the rules at your address.

name: Pennsylvania
publisher: Pennsylvania DCNR, DEP and local authorities

extraUrls.label: Municipal boundaries of Pennsylvania air basins

notes: County officials can issue temporary bans. Carbon County publishes municipal burning statuses, and Pike County dispatch lists active local bans. Many county results show standing city, township or air-basin rules. Check the named jurisdiction and activities on your county result, and check the date on DCNR's county map.

name: Rhode Island
publisher: Rhode Island DEM and local fire authorities

extraUrls.label: State park and management area fire rules
State air-quality rules for open fires

notes: Rhode Island requires written permits for covered burning on state property or on or near forest land. State parks have separate fire rules. The Governor and DEM have emergency powers, and towns and fire districts set local rules. We track standing state rules and the published rules for Narragansett, North Kingstown and South Kingstown. Ask your local fire department or land manager about temporary orders and permits for your site.

name: South Carolina
publisher: South Carolina Forestry Commission and Department of Environmental Services

extraUrls.label: State Forestry Commission orders and lifts
State bans and Red Flag Fire Alerts
Horry County Fire Rescue open-burning rules

notes: The State Forester or Governor can issue temporary burn bans outside city and town limits. We check the Forestry Commission for current residential yard-debris closures and track state limits on land-clearing and residential construction burns. Check the state notices and your local fire department for other orders and the rules for your location.

name: South Dakota
publisher: County emergency management, South Dakota Wildland Fire and BLM South Dakota Field Office

extraUrls.label: Black Hills burn permit rules and district map
BLM fire restrictions and signed orders
Black Hills National Forest fire restrictions
South Dakota air quality rules for open burning
South Dakota Grassland Fire Danger Index

notes: County emergency managers and commissions publish local burn bans. Selected county and municipal reports cover standing permit or notification rules. Check the local fire authority and land manager for conditions at the burn site.

name: Tennessee
publisher: Tennessee Division of Forestry

extraUrls.label: Tennessee burn permits and seasonal rules
Tennessee air-quality rules for open burning
Shelby County open burning and land clearing

notes: Covered burns can require state permits from October 15 through May 15. County and city fire or air-quality offices may add restrictions. Check the listed agencies for your address and activity.

name: Texas
publisher: Texas A&M Forest Service
notes: Texas A&M Forest Service republishes county orders it receives. County orders generally apply to unincorporated areas. Confirm timing, area and any discrepancies with the issuing county.

name: Utah
publisher: Utah Division of Forestry, Fire and State Lands

extraUrls.label: Utah county and city burn permits

notes: The state forester issues fire restrictions on state and unincorporated private lands. Cities, tribal governments and federal land managers set rules for their own jurisdictions. County and city fire authorities handle residential burn permits, and Utah DEQ sets separate seasonal and air-quality rules. Check the order for your location.

name: Vermont
publisher: Vermont Department of Forests, Parks and Recreation
notes: Town forest fire wardens or their deputies issue permits for covered burning and can restrict it locally. The state can issue broader orders. Check with your local warden for current restrictions and permit exceptions. Vermont DEC also limits what you can burn.

name: Virginia
publisher: Virginia Department of Forestry, local fire authorities, and public land managers

extraUrls.label: Virginia DEQ open burning rules and local ordinances
Shenandoah National Park alerts and conditions
Fairfax County recreational fires and open burning

notes: Virginia coverage combines monitored local notices, standing local restrictions and public-land orders. From February 15 through April 30, Virginia limits when you can start a covered fire near woodland, brushland or dry fields. The Governor can issue emergency orders. Check your local fire marshal and the land manager for your address or burn site.

name: Washington
publisher: Washington Department of Ecology

extraUrls.label: Puget Sound air quality burn ban status
King County fire safety burn bans
Northwest Clean Air Agency burn ban status
Southwest Washington county burning status and maps

notes: Washington coverage includes local county, fire district and clean air agency reports as well as standing permit and no-burn rules. DNR sets fire safety restrictions on land it protects. Check the agency for your address, land manager and the kind of burning you plan.

name: West Virginia
publisher: West Virginia Division of Forestry

extraUrls.label: West Virginia DEP open burning rules

notes: West Virginia limits covered outdoor burning statewide from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern in March–May and October–December. The Forestry director can issue emergency bans with the Governor's approval. Ask Forestry and your local fire authority about current orders, permits and rules at your address.

name: Wisconsin
publisher: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources
notes: The DNR posts debris-burning permit limits and suspensions for its fire protection areas. Check WisBURN after 9 a.m. Central on the day you plan to burn. County results also show verified local rules and orders where available. Check the jurisdiction named in the report and ask your fire department about your address.

Wisconsin county and municipal ordinance directory
City of Madison burning rules and permits

name: Wyoming
publisher: Wyoming State Forestry Division and Wyoming Office of State Lands and Investments

extraUrls.label: Wyoming air-quality and burn permit rules
Rocky Mountain interagency fire restrictions map

notes: County commissioners issue orders for specific areas, and State Forestry maps the orders it receives. Check the latest order with the county fire warden. Open fires are limited year-round on state trust lands. Towns, fire districts, tribal authorities and federal land managers may have their own rules. Wyoming DEQ has separate air-quality and burn permit requirements.
